local.bun-cli:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/katisfaktion/loadouts/v0.1.0/schemas/v1/loadout.schema.json
name: bun-cli
items:
  verification:
    conventions: |
      Run bun test before committing. For CLI integration tests, use a temporary HOME, a fixture catalog and fake installers; keep network calls and the developer's agent setup out of the test.
  interface:
    packageSkills:
      include: ["@optique/core#optique"]
    conventions: |
      When changing a CLI command, keep its help, exit codes and machine-readable output consistent. Add a Changeset for user-visible behavior changes.
  tooling:
    skills: [laurigates/claude-plugins@bun-development]
routing:
  - when: Selecting bun test flags or building and cross-compiling the standalone CLI
    use: [tooling]
  - when: Adding or changing CLI commands, options or argument parsing with Optique
    use: [interface]
local.github-contributions:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/katisfaktion/loadouts/v0.1.0/schemas/v1/loadout.schema.json
name: github-contributions
items:
  github:
    skills: [cli/cli@gh]
    conventions: |
      Before drafting or submitting a GitHub issue, read the matching form in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and address its required fields. For PRs, read .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and keep its headings. Follow the template even when supplying a body directly to gh or an API. A request for a draft ends with a title and body.
  writing:
    skills: [cursor/plugins@unslop]
    conventions: Edit the prose without changing template headings, quoted errors, commands, or reported test results.
  commits:
    skills: [github/awesome-copilot@git-commit]
    conventions: |
      Give each commit one purpose and a Conventional Commits subject. Before submitting a PR, review the commits against its target branch. Fold fixups and work-in-progress commits into the changes they complete, split unrelated changes, and order the series so a reviewer can follow it. Verify the final diff and rerun the project checks after rewriting. Get approval before rewriting published history.
routing:
  - when: Drafting or revising a GitHub issue or pull request
    use: [github, writing]
  - when: Writing or editing contribution docs, Changesets, commit messages or review comments
    use: [writing]
  - when: Creating or splitting commits for a contribution
    use: [commits, writing]
